entries.description: Stand-up special. Pryor voices objects, animals and absent people rather than describing them, which converts autobiography into dialogue and…
entries.text: Stand-up special. Pryor voices objects, animals and absent people rather than describing them, which converts autobiography into dialogue and removes the audience's option to pity him. The material is unsparing about his own conduct and never asks for sympathy, which earns the licence for everything else in the set. It is the most-imitated hour in the form and the point at which American stand-up became a writer's medium.

entries.name: Class Clown
entries.author: George Carlin
entries.awards: None. The album holds no Grammy; the 1973 Best Comedy Recording went to Carlin's FM & AM, a different record. Class Clown was added to the National Recording Registry in 2015, which is a preservation selection rather than an award.
entries.description: Comedy album. The record containing the seven-words routine, which reached the United States Supreme Court in a broadcasting case and remains the…
entries.text: Comedy album. The record containing the seven-words routine, which reached the United States Supreme Court in a broadcasting case and remains the most legally consequential piece of American stand-up. Carlin takes phrases used without examination and reverses their moral loading, then holds the reversal long enough for the audience to feel the original assumption. The persona shifts across his career from observer to prosecutor, and this is the hinge.

entries.name: The Button-Down Mind of Bob Newhart
entries.author: Bob Newhart
entries.awards: Grammy Award for Album of the Year, the first comedy record to win it, and Best New Artist — the latter awarded to Newhart as an artist rather than to the album. The 1961 comedy award went to the sequel, The Button-Down Mind Strikes Back!, under the category name Best Comedy Performance, Spoken Word. Grammy's own site retroactively relabels all of these Best Comedy Album, a category that did not then exist.
entries.description: Comedy album. One-sided telephone routines in which the unheard half is supplied entirely by the listener. The pauses are the content and their…
entries.text: Comedy album. One-sided telephone routines in which the unheard half is supplied entirely by the listener. The pauses are the content and their length is the joke, which makes this the most economical demonstration in the form that a comic pause carries information rather than merely spacing a line. It is unperformable on the page, and it made the comedy album a commercial format.

entries.name: Bring the Pain
entries.author: Chris Rock
entries.awards: Two Primetime Emmy Awards in 1997; the award for Outstanding Variety, Music or Comedy Special went to its producers. The Grammy frequently attached to this special was in fact won by the 1997 album Roll with the New, under the category name Best Spoken Comedy Album.
entries.description: Stand-up special. Rock installs each premise by making the audience state it silently through a rhetorical question, then contradicts the position…
entries.text: Stand-up special. Rock installs each premise by making the audience state it silently through a rhetorical question, then contradicts the position he has just had them adopt. The technique makes the audience the payer without their noticing, and it is why the hardest material lands with rooms that would refuse the same content stated flatly. The special is generally treated as the point at which his persona settled.

entries.name: Inside
entries.author: Bo Burnham
entries.awards: Three Primetime Emmy Awards in 2021, all to Burnham alone — Directing for a Variety Special, Writing for a Variety Special, and Music Direction. It lost Outstanding Variety Special, Pre-Recorded. Grammy Award for Best Song Written for Visual Media at the 64th ceremony, to Burnham as songwriter for All Eyes on Me — not a comedy category.
entries.description: Stand-up special. Written, performed, shot and edited alone in one room across a year of confinement. Burnham makes the construction of the work its…
entries.text: Stand-up special. Written, performed, shot and edited alone in one room across a year of confinement. Burnham makes the construction of the work its subject, so the audience watches it being assembled and degrading simultaneously; several songs end without a button, which is a deliberately dead beat rather than a failure. Earlier material returns in worse condition, which expresses the passage of time structurally rather than stating it.

entries.name: Delirious
entries.author: Eddie Murphy
entries.awards: None. The 1984 Grammy for Best Comedy Recording went to the album Eddie Murphy: Comedian, a different work.
entries.description: Stand-up special. A twenty-two-year-old performing to a large arena at very high physical energy, with full-body act-outs switched rapidly. It is a…
entries.text: Stand-up special. A twenty-two-year-old performing to a large arena at very high physical energy, with full-body act-outs switched rapidly. It is a live contested case on its homophobic opening material: criticised at the time and again on its 2016 streaming release, with Murphy issuing a written apology in 1996 and separately describing the material as ignorant in a 2019 interview. Those are two distinct speech acts made two decades apart, and the pack states both and adjudicates neither.

entries.name: The Goon Show
entries.author: Spike Milligan
entries.awards: None located. No award record was found for the programme, which is a documentation gap rather than a verified negative.
entries.description: Radio series. Half-hours in which causation is optional and the only continuity is voice. Milligan wrote almost all of it single-handed and suffered…
entries.text: Radio series. Half-hours in which causation is optional and the only continuity is voice. Milligan wrote almost all of it single-handed and suffered a breakdown during the run; the surrealism was possible precisely because radio requires nothing to be depicted. It established that a comic form could dispense with plot entirely if the invention is internally consistent, and its influence on the following generation of British comedy is close to total.

entries.name: Round the Horne
entries.author: Barry Took and Marty Feldman
entries.awards: None located for this programme. A Writers' Guild award sometimes attached to it belongs to Took and Feldman's series Marty.
entries.description: Radio series. A sketch programme whose innuendo density is a direct product of broadcasting restriction: what could not be stated had to be…
entries.text: Radio series. A sketch programme whose innuendo density is a direct product of broadcasting restriction: what could not be stated had to be constructed, and the construction is the comedy. Its two most famous characters spoke Polari, a coded gay argot, on the BBC in years when homosexuality was criminal in England and Wales, which put an underground vocabulary into a mainstream Sunday audience without ever naming what it was.

entries.name: The Sitcom's Broadcast Commission
entries.description: The multi-camera/single-camera production form, the studio audience, and the episode order — owned by the tv-formats-reference pack.
entries.principle: This pack's §4 originally declined to write this card: the sitcom's structure was Comedy's central claim and could not be lent out before a pack existed to own the other half of it. That pack now exists. The seam is production against joke: a multi-camera sitcom shot before a live studio audience on a four-camera setup, and a single-camera sitcom shot like a small film with no audience signal at all, are two different commissioning decisions that change what a script can do before a single joke is written — the beat length a live audience's laugh imposes, the coverage a single camera affords instead. That decision, the episode order it is commissioned in, and the broadcast season it is scheduled against belong to tv-formats-reference. What stays here is the joke itself: the runner, the reaction shot's timing, the premise's comic engine — the thing the production form is built to deliver, not the delivery apparatus.
entries.example: *Frasier* and *Arrested Development* can share almost every structural joke-craft card in this pack's Craft collection and still be produced under opposite disciplines — one in front of an audience whose laugh sets the beat, one in total control of rhythm via the edit — and that difference is tv-formats-reference's to carry, not this pack's.
entries.application: For the joke, the runner, and the reaction signal, work here. For which production form a sitcom is commissioned under, its episode order, and its season's broadcast shape, go to tv-formats-reference.
